subject: Acme POC: success criteria & eval methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Acme POC: success criteria & eval methodology

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion and very clear priorities. Per request, here’s a concise recap and a proposed POC/eval plan so we can align on success criteria, ownership, and timeline.

Summary of priorities (from Acme):
- Improve customer support response quality (factuality + helpfulness)
- Keep inference latency < 400ms P95 for interactive use cases
- Stay within a cost envelope (target: <$0.60 per 1k tokens consumed)
- No sensitive data retained beyond session (data retention + audit logs)

Proposed POC approach:
1) Offline evaluation (May 11–17): Redwood runs an offline eval on a shared prompt set + a redacted sample of your production transcripts. We’ll use a grading rubric (see attached) with metrics: accuracy/helpfulness, safety pass rate, and relevance.
2) Online shadow / small-scale live (May 18–24): Shadow traffic routing for real-world signals (latency, false positives, human override rate).
3) Decision & next steps (by May 25): go/no-go + next steps for procurement.

Success criteria (draft - please adjust):
- Helpfulness: human eval average >= 3.8/5
- Safety: zero high-severity safety failures across a 200-sample audit
- Latency: P95 < 400ms (end-to-end, from request to token stream)
- Cost: expected token cost <= $0.60 per 1k tokens

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood: Marissa (stakeholder comms + project lead), Rachel (eval design + grading), Dev (integration, infra checks)
- Acme: Alice (product sponsor), Tom (technical lead), Security (security sign-off), Procurement (contracting)

Attachments: acme-poc-success-criteria.xlsx, eval-grading-rubric.md
Related doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1acme-eval-plan

Next steps for Acme: please confirm the owners above and share a redacted sample of transcripts (or 100–200 example prompts) by May 13 so Rachel can finalize the rubric and we can start offline evals on May 11.

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation and any edits to the success criteria.

--
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 
1) Offline eval vs online shadow: can you outline what differences we should expect in scores? For example, should we expect measured helpfulness to be higher in offline tests than in shadowed live traffic?
2) Latency: the 400ms p95 target — is that for the model only, or end-to-end including our application (we have additional routing/transform steps)?
3) Cost: does the $0.60 per 1k token include both prompt + response tokens? We need that number to be comparable to our internal benchmarks.
4) Security: our InfoSec will want a SOC2 artifact and confirmation on data retention settings. Can you share the envelope for the shadow environment (i.e., will any raw transcripts leave our VPC)?

We can get a redacted sample to you by May 13. Procurement will likely want a statement of work before committing resources — looping them here.

Tom
Engineering Manager, Acme

Thanks — quick note from the eval side so Acme knows what to expect. I’ve attached a short grading rubric (eval-grading-rubric.md) but the highlights below are what I’ll use for the offline run: 

Evaluation metrics (offline):
- Helpfulness (human-annotated, 1–5): target >= 3.8
- Correctness / factuality (binary per sample) / factuality rate target >= 92%
- Safety: classification into (pass/flag) with zero high-severity flags in the audit sample
- Relevance: top-1 retrieval match rate for retrieval-augmented prompts
- Latency (model-only in offline synthetic runs): measured to validate perf baseline but primary E2E latency will come from shadow run
- Cost estimate: computed from tokens produced in the offline samples to project per-1k cost

Offline vs Online note: offline evals are useful for quality and regressions; they generally produce cleaner and often slightly higher yardsticks since annotators don’t have production context or time pressure. The online shadow run is the definitive test for latency, reliability, and cost under real traffic and is where we expect to see final numbers.

Sampling plan: we’ll run offline on 500 samples (350 curated prompts + 150 redacted production samples). For human evals I’ll sample 200 of the 500 for double-annotator review.

Let me know if Acme wants to adjust the sample sizes or grading thresholds. I’ll kick off the offline run once we receive the prompt set.

Cheers,
Rachel Kim
Evaluation Lead, Redwood Inference

Couple quick technical notes from infra/SE side: 
- Recommended model variant: Redwood-falcon-1.0-quant (good balance of quality/cost). Will validate memory footprint during smoke tests.
- KV cache & batching: we’ll enable small batching (50–100ms window) and prefix KV caching for repeated session context to hit latency targets.
- Sample data ingestion: please provide a redacted transcript file in ndjson (one JSON per line) or CSV; we can accept up to 2GB for the offline run but prefer a 100–200 sample subset initially.
- Network: need a VPN endpoint + egress IP allowlist for the shadow environment — see attached network-requirements.pdf.

I can run smoke tests May 12–13 and share infra-checklist.pdf outputs. If Acme can provide a 50-sample test set today/tomorrow, I’ll validate end-to-end connectivity and a quick latency baseline.

—Dev
